title: Config Lab: Recommendation Audit Trail & Explainable Tuning
creator: Evan Brooks
description: Create a lightweight Config Lab screen in Redwood Console for operators to inspect, evaluate, and iteratively tune caching and batching recommendations. The Lab focuses on three capabilities: 1) an explainable recommendation panel that shows why a suggestion was made (latency/cost trade-offs, workload signals), 2) an immutable audit trail of recommendation changes and who applied them, and 3) a sandbox toggle to simulate policy impact before committing (guardrails + quick rollback). The experience should be geared toward platform engineers and SREs who want confidence before applying autoscaling/batching/caching changes to Dedicated and Private deployments.
user_stories: As an infra engineer, I want to see the rationale behind a batching recommendation so I can approve it with confidence.
As a platform owner, I want an audit trail of recommendation changes and which user applied them for compliance reviews.
As an operator, I want to simulate a recommended cache TTL and batching window against sampled traces before applying it to production.
As a PM, I want an integrated CTA that converts an accepted simulation to a rollout plan (canary + fallback).
design_proposals: Panelized layout: left column - workload selector + historical perf summary; middle - explainable recommendation card with signal breakdown; right - sandbox simulator with time slider and estimated cost delta.
Recommendation card components: score (confidence), dominant signal tags (long tail seqs, bursty QPS), expected latency % change, cost delta per 10k tokens, and recommended guardrail presets.
Audit trail: chronologically ordered entries with user, timestamp, previous & proposed config diff, explanation text, link to simulation snapshot, and a reversible action (rollback to prior config).
Simulation engine UX: sample window selector (last 1h, 24h, custom), sliders for TTL/batch size/latency SLO, and a visualized per-token cost curve to make trade-offs tangible.
CTA: 'Open Rollout' button pre-populates canary policy modal in the Rollouts flow; includes suggested metrics to monitor (p99 latency, token cost, error rate).
comments: 2025-02-14 - Jonah Park (Eng): Reviewed early wireframes. Feels good; need to confirm data availability for per-10k token cost; backend will need an API that returns simulated deltas for arbitrary TTL/batch settings.
2025-02-20 - Maya Chen (Design): Iterated prototype to include confidence score explanation chips ("kernel mismatch", "kv cache hit rate") per feedback from Research.
2025-02-25 - Priya Ramesh (PM): Requested that audit trail entries include config hashes for easier mapping to infra audit logs; added as acceptance criteria.
2025-02-28 - SRE Rotation (note): Simulation engine must never run against live production writes; use sampled read-only traces and capped token budgets. See incident playbook link in Confluence.
2025-03-03 - Security (review): Reviewed data in audit trail for PII; approved with note to redact prompt content and only display aggregated signal metadata.

2025-03-05 - Design Review: Prototype walkthrough with Eng and PM. Agreed to split work into two sprints: MVP (explainable recommendation card + audit trail entries) and Sprint+1 (full simulator + rollout integration).
decisions: MVP scope: build explainable recommendation card and immutable audit trail. Simulator and rollout integration deferred to next sprint.
Recommendation rationale will surface aggregate signals (e.g., 'median seq length', 'cache hit %') but will not show raw prompt/token content to avoid leaking user data.
Audit trail entries will be write-once and include a reversible config pointer rather than storing full config blobs in the UI datastore.
acceptance_criteria: Design mockups completed for MVP screens (recommendation card + audit trail) with responsive states for console width variants.
Prototype validated in design review with Eng and PM and recorded feedback captured in comments.
Frontend acceptance tests cover rendering of recommendation rationale chips and audit trail diffs.
Backend API contract documented: /v1/configlab/simulate and /v1/configlab/recommendations endpoints with example payloads.
Security sign-off confirming no raw prompt content is surfaced in the audit trail or recommendation explanation.
risks: Data completeness: recommendation engine may not have strong signals for low-traffic workloads, leading to low-confidence recommendations.
Cost simulation accuracy depends on precise kernel selection and quantization assumptions; mismatch could mislead operators.
UX complexity: exposing too many knobs in the Lab risks confusing users; guardrail presets are required to keep defaults safe.
Privacy: accidental exposure of prompt content in trace samples if engineering controls are not enforced.
